name: risk_classifier
intended_use: Estimate the probability that a helpee's current device context contains sensitive content, so the adaptive policy engine can select an assistance mode. Output is a suggestion bounded by the rule-based safety envelope.
out_of_scope_use: Must not be used to grant a capability the rule envelope forbids, to make any decision without the helpee's explicit consent, or as evidence about a person's behaviour or trustworthiness.
training_data: Synthetic contexts from ml.datasets.generators with a documented generative process. No real user data was used or is available; see docs/ML_METHODOLOGY.md.
limitations: Trained entirely on synthetic data. Reported metrics describe the simulator, not real usage.
Features are supplied by the client and are therefore attacker-influenceable; the rule envelope keys on OS-provided signals for this reason.
Calibration is expected to drift as the app population changes; recalibrate against production data before relying on the probability.
Abstains on the cost-equivalence band (0.08363636363636363, 0.09818181818181819), where the rule engine decides instead.
ethical_considerations: Errors are asymmetric by design: a false 'safe' can expose an elderly person's financial data, so the threshold is set from a 10:1 cost ratio rather than at 0.5.
The model never grants a capability; it can only propose one at or below the rule ceiling.
Decisions are logged with their features so any outcome can be explained to the person it affected.
